title: Jacobean context
learning_objectives: Explain who James I was and why the Gunpowder Plot and witchcraft mattered to the original audience; begin a quotation web
key_content: James I and the Divine Right of Kings; the Gunpowder Plot (1605); Daemonologie and Jacobean beliefs about witchcraft; regicide as the ultimate crime
teaching_approach: Context taught before the play, then returned to in every week; pupils start a quotation web they add to all term

title: Act 1: ambition and Lady Macbeth
learning_objectives: Analyse how Shakespeare presents Macbeth's ambition and Lady Macbeth's manipulation through single-word zoom-in
key_content: Act 1 scenes 1–7; 'Stars, hide your fires'; 'unsex me here'; 'look like th' innocent flower'; darkness imagery; soliloquy and aside
teaching_approach: Zoom-in word analysis (what, how, why) modelled on 'black and deep desires'; hot-seating Lady Macbeth

title: Act 2: guilt and blood
learning_objectives: Analyse blood and sleep imagery as presentations of guilt; avoid naming a technique without its effect
key_content: Act 2 scenes 1–3; the dagger soliloquy; 'Neptune's ocean'; 'Macbeth does murder sleep'
teaching_approach: Zoom-in on 'all' and 'great'; explicit 'common mistake' slot: 'Shakespeare uses blood imagery' and stops

title: Acts 3 and 4: appearance and reality; are the witches to blame?
learning_objectives: Track appearance and reality across Acts 3–4; weigh two readings of the witches' influence using Banquo as contrast
key_content: Act 3 (Banquo's murder, the banquet, 'full of scorpions'); Act 4 (the apparitions, Macduff's family); dramatic irony; 'There's daggers in men's smiles'; fate and free will
teaching_approach: Debate: the witches control Macbeth versus he chooses; plan both readings before deciding

title: Thesis-led writing
learning_objectives: Write a thesis-led response that moves from the extract to the whole play and uses context purposefully
key_content: Thesis statement; extract-to-whole-play structure; context that earns its place (Gunpowder Plot linked to regicide)
teaching_approach: Thesis-first planning; no formulaic paragraph templates; context folded into the sentence it supports

title: Act 5: Lady Macbeth's collapse
learning_objectives: Analyse the sleepwalking scene as the reversal of Act 1 Lady Macbeth; compare verse and prose
key_content: Act 5 scene 1; 'Out, damned spot'; prose versus verse; the character arc from 'unsex me' to sleepwalking
teaching_approach: Zoom-in on the prose; character arc timeline drawn across Acts 1 and 5
assessment: Paragraph comparing Act 1 and Act 5 Lady Macbeth

title: Act 5: the ending and the tragic hero
learning_objectives: Evaluate 'this dead butcher' as a verdict on Macbeth; apply the tragic-hero structure
key_content: Act 5 scenes 3–9; 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow'; Malcolm's 'dead butcher'; Shakespearean tragedy and the tragic hero; rise and fall
teaching_approach: Debate the verdict; thesis-led essay planning on the whole play
assessment: Full essay (45 min), end of unit
